title: Cohesion & Coherence
description: Master cohesion and coherence for Grade 11: reference, substitution, ellipsis, conjunction, lexical cohesion, topic sentences and logical sequencing — bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Cohesion — The Links Between Sentences
topics.concept:
Cohesion uses five main devices to connect sentences:

  • Reference: pronouns and demonstratives point back to a noun — Riya won. She was thrilled. This surprised no one.
  • Substitution: a pro-form replaces a phrase — I need a pen. Do you have one?
  • Ellipsis: repeated words are omitted — She passed; he didn't (pass).
  • Conjunction: connectors show the relation — however, therefore, moreover, in addition.
  • Lexical cohesion: repetition, synonyms and collocation keep a theme alive — the forest … the woods … these trees.

These links are what stop a paragraph from feeling like a list of unrelated sentences.

examples.problem: Which cohesion device links these? The minister spoke. He sounded confident.
Identify the device: Some students passed; others did not.

recap: Cohesion devices: reference, substitution, ellipsis, conjunction, lexical
Reference (he/this) and conjunctions (however/therefore) are the most common
Lexical cohesion keeps a theme alive with synonyms and repetition

topics.title: Coherence — The Logic of Ideas
topics.concept:
Coherence is about the order and logic of ideas, not just surface links. A coherent paragraph has:

  • A clear topic sentence that states the main idea.
  • Supporting details that develop that idea, each relevant.
  • A logical sequence — chronological, cause-effect, general-to-specific, or order of importance.
  • Smooth transitions between points (first, then, as a result, finally).

A paragraph can be cohesive (full of connectors) yet incoherent if the ideas don't actually follow. Coherence asks: does each sentence belong here, and in this order?

To improve coherence: start with the topic sentence, group related ideas, cut anything off-topic, and order the points so the reader is never lost.

examples.problem:
Which is the topic sentence?
(a) For example, sleep improves memory.
(b) Good sleep is essential for health.
examples.solution: (b) — it states the main idea; (a) is a supporting detail.

examples.problem: Order for coherence: (1) As a result, the plants died. (2) The gardener forgot to water them. (3) The summer was unusually hot.

recap: Coherence = logical order of ideas, not just surface links
Topic sentence + relevant supporting details + logical sequence
Use transitions; cut off-topic sentences; order points clearly

questions.q: Coherence concerns:
'This' pointing back to a sentence is which device?
Which is the topic sentence?
Best connector: 'He trained hard; ___ , he won.'
Which device omits repeated words?
'I want a red one' — 'one' is:
Which keeps a theme with synonyms?
A paragraph that jumps between unrelated ideas lacks:
Best transition for sequence: 'Plan first. ___ , write.'
Which improves cohesion?
questions.explanation: Clear reference and connectors link sentences.

questions.q: Which sentence has vague reference?
options: Riya called Sara, and she answered. (unclear 'she')

questions.q: Topic sentence + details + logical order create:
Order for coherence: (P) Consequently, sales doubled. (Q) The company redesigned its product. (R) Customers responded enthusiastically. (S) It also lowered the price.
Which revision best improves cohesion? 'The scheme helped farmers. Farmers earned more. Farmers were happy.'
options: The scheme helped farmers, who earned more and were therefore happy.
Helped the scheme farmers happy were.
questions.explanation: Reference ('who') and a connector ('therefore') replace clumsy repetition.

questions.q: Identify the off-topic sentence in a paragraph about healthy eating:
options: My uncle owns a cricket bat.
questions.explanation: The cricket bat sentence is irrelevant — it breaks coherence.

questions.q: Which connector signals a conclusion?
Best topic sentence for a paragraph listing causes of traffic jams:
options: Several factors cause traffic jams in our city.

questions.q: Which sentence uses lexical cohesion effectively?
options: The dog barked. The dog ran. The dog ate. The dog slept.
The puppy barked; the little animal then darted across the yard.
Dog the barked ran the dog.
questions.explanation: Synonyms ('puppy', 'little animal') keep the theme without monotony.

questions.q: Choose the most coherent sequence: (1) Hence, the bridge collapsed. (2) Engineers warned of the cracks. (3) The warnings were ignored.
Which improves both cohesion and coherence?
options: Adding a topic sentence and linking details with appropriate connectors in a logical order.
Making every sentence the same length.
questions.explanation: A clear topic sentence (coherence) plus apt connectors (cohesion) in logical order.

outcomes: Distinguish cohesion (the links) from coherence (the logic)
Use reference, substitution, ellipsis and conjunction to link ideas
Write a clear topic sentence with supporting details

intro.en: Good writing doesn't just have correct sentences — it holds together. Cohesion is the set of grammatical and lexical links that tie sentences (pronouns, connectors, repeated key words). Coherence is the deeper logic — ideas in a sensible order, each building on the last. Cohesion is the stitching; coherence is the shape of the garment.
intro.hi: अच्छे लेखन में केवल सही वाक्य नहीं होते — वह आपस में जुड़ा रहता है। Cohesion उन व्याकरणिक व शाब्दिक कड़ियों का समूह है जो वाक्यों को बाँधती हैं (सर्वनाम, संयोजक, दोहराए मुख्य शब्द)। Coherence गहरा तर्क है — विचार समझदार क्रम में, हर एक पिछले पर आधारित। Cohesion सिलाई है; coherence वस्त्र का आकार।

real_life.situation:
Two versions of a short note:

Disjointed: Trees are important. People cut forests. Air is polluted. We should plant.

Cohesive: Trees are important because they clean the air. However, people keep cutting forests, so pollution rises. Therefore, we should plant more.
real_life.why: The second version adds links ('because', 'However', 'so', 'Therefore') and keeps the topic (trees/air) running through it. The ideas now flow logically — that combination of cohesion and coherence is what makes writing read well.

Lexicalforest… trees… woodland
rule_box.formula: Cohesion = the links between sentences · Coherence = the logical order of ideas
rule_box.example: Pollution is rising. This (reference) worries scientists, who (reference) urge action.

quick_test.explanation: Coherence concerns how logically the ideas are connected and ordered.

common_mistakes.wrong: A paragraph with connectors but no logical order.
common_mistakes.right: Order the ideas logically AND link them.
common_mistakes.note: Cohesion without coherence still confuses the reader.

common_mistakes.wrong: Starting a paragraph with an example, not a topic sentence.
common_mistakes.right: Begin with a clear topic sentence.

common_mistakes.wrong: Using 'it'/'this' with no clear noun to refer to.
Repeating the same word too often instead of using synonyms.
common_mistakes.note: Lexical cohesion needs variety, not monotony.

error_detection.sentence: The dog barked. It was angry. It scared. It ran.
error_detection.correct: The dog barked angrily. It scared the children and then ran off.
Sleep is important. However, many people ignore it.

error_detection.sentence: He studied. He played. He slept. He ate. He worked.
error_detection.correct: He studied in the morning, then played, and after a meal he worked late.

sentence_correction.wrong: The plan failed therefore we tried again moreover we learned.
sentence_correction.correct: The plan failed; therefore, we tried again. Moreover, we learned from it.

sentence_correction.wrong: Reading is good. Cricket is fun. Maths is hard. (no link)
sentence_correction.correct: Reading is good for the mind, just as exercise like cricket is good for the body.

(1) She practised daily. (2) Riya wanted to win. (3) Finally, she succeeded.
(1) However, it was too late. (2) We rushed to the station. (3) The train had left.

reading.passage: Plastic pollution is a growing crisis. It harms oceans, kills marine life, and enters our food. However, the problem is not hopeless. Many cities have banned single-use bags; others are encouraging recycling. Moreover, new materials are being developed. Therefore, with awareness and effort, this damage can still be reversed. In short, the solution lies in our own hands.

questions.q: Identify the topic sentence.
questions.answer: 'Plastic pollution is a growing crisis.' — it states the main idea.

questions.q: Find two conjunctions used for cohesion and the relation each shows.
Give one example of lexical cohesion in the passage.
questions.answer: 'pollution … the problem … this damage … the solution' keep the theme connected.

speaking: Trees clean the air; moreover, they give shade.
She studied hard; therefore, she passed.
It rained; however, we still went out.
First we planned, then we acted.
In short, hard work pays off.

writing.prompt: Write a short coherent paragraph (5 sentences) on any topic, beginning with a clear topic sentence, then supporting details linked with at least three cohesion devices.
writing.example: Reading is a powerful habit. It widens our knowledge and sharpens the mind. Moreover, it improves our language. However, fewer people read today. Therefore, we must revive this habit.
